prompts.tools.purpose.detailed: Explain what [tool] is for to someone who hasn't used it yet. Structure: what it does in one sentence, 3 typical tasks, what it's not suited for, what's needed to start (account, device). If you're unsure about anything, especially pricing or availability in [country], say so and suggest checking the official site.
prompts.tools.purpose.refine: Explain it even more simply, with an example from a student's life.
prompts.tools.purpose.check: Here's my understanding: [my understanding]. Have I got the right idea of what the tool does?
prompts.tools.tasks.short: What typical tasks is [tool] used for?
prompts.tools.tasks.detailed: List 8 typical tasks for [tool] for [who I am: school student, university student, professional]. For each: an example prompt, the result to expect, what to watch for when checking it. Separately, 3 tasks where another tool would be better, and what kind of tool.
prompts.tools.tasks.refine: Pick the 3 tasks that are best for getting started.
prompts.tools.tasks.check: I tried [task] and the result was [result]. Is that normal or am I doing something wrong?
prompts.tools.first.short: Help me write my first prompt for [tool] for this task: [task]
prompts.tools.first.detailed: I'm using [tool] for the first time. Task: [task]. Write a first prompt using: role or context, goal, input (no personal data), answer format, constraints. Explain why each part is there. Add 2 follow-up prompts to send after the first answer.
prompts.tools.first.refine: The answer was too general: [answer]. How should I refine the prompt?
prompts.tools.first.check: Here's my prompt: [prompt]. What's missing for a more useful answer?
prompts.tools.compare.detailed: Compare [tool 1] and [tool 2] for [task]. Table: what it can do for this task, what working with it looks like, strengths, limitations, what's needed to start. For pricing, limits and availability in [country], write “check the official site” if unsure. Don't pick a winner for me: say which is handier in which situation.
prompts.tools.compare.refine: How can I compare them myself on the same task? Suggest a test prompt.
prompts.tools.compare.check: I tried both. Here are the results: [results]. What criteria should I judge them by?
prompts.tools.check.short: What should I check in [tool]'s answers for [task]?
prompts.tools.check.detailed: I use [tool] for [task]. Make a checklist for checking its answers: typical errors for this kind of tool in this task (invented facts and links, outdated data, calculation errors, mistranslated terms, distorted meaning), how to spot each, what to check against.
prompts.tools.check.refine: Make a short 5-point version I can keep at hand.
prompts.tools.check.check: Go through the checklist with this answer: [answer]. What raises doubts?
prompts.tools.settings.short: Which [tool] settings should I check at the start?
prompts.tools.settings.detailed: I'm starting to use [tool]. Which types of settings should I check first: interface language, chat history and saving, use of my data for training, access to files and apps, notifications, sign-in security. For each, why to check it. If you don't know exactly what the setting is called in this tool, say so and suggest searching the help pages.
prompts.tools.settings.refine: Write search queries to find these settings in the official help.
prompts.tools.settings.check: I found the setting [setting] set to [value]. What does that mean for my data?
prompts.tools.safe.short: How can I start using [tool] safely?
prompts.tools.safe.detailed: Make a plan for safely getting started with [tool]: how to make sure it's the official site or app, what password to choose, whether to turn on two-factor authentication, what data not to put in prompts, how to check age restrictions, what to do if asked for payment or access to contacts. If you don't know this tool's specifics, give general rules.
prompts.tools.safe.refine: Make a version for parents helping a child get started.
prompts.tools.safe.check: The tool asked for [what it asked for]. Is that normal or suspicious?
prompts.tools.plan.short: What in [tool] might depend on the plan and the country?
prompts.tools.plan.detailed: Help me understand what in [tool] can vary by plan, country ([country]) and user age. Table: what might differ (limits, features, languages, model access, data retention), why, where to check it on the official site. Don't give specific prices or limits unless you're sure.
prompts.tools.plan.refine: Will the free version be enough for [task]? What should I ask myself?
prompts.tools.plan.check: Here's what the official page says: [text]. Explain it in plain words.
prompts.tools.official.short: Where can I find official information about [tool]?
prompts.tools.official.detailed: Tell me how to find official sources on [tool]: which sections developers usually have (help, documentation, pricing, privacy policy, terms of use, an updates blog), how to tell the official site from a fake, which search queries to use. Don't make up page addresses.
prompts.tools.official.refine: Help me read the privacy policy: which sections should I look at first?
prompts.tools.official.check: Here's the address I found: [address]. How can I check it's the official site?
prompts.tools.changes.short: The [feature] in [tool] doesn't work like it used to. What should I do?
prompts.tools.changes.detailed: In [tool], the [feature] used to work like this: [how it was], and now: [how it is]. Help me figure it out: possible causes (an update, a different plan or region, settings, a bug), what to check in order, where to find official information about changes, what workarounds exist. Don't claim the feature was removed unless you're sure.
prompts.tools.changes.refine: Help me write a short message to support about the issue, without personal data.
prompts.tools.changes.check: Which other tool could replace this feature if it doesn't come back?

verify.tools.purpose: AI may not know about new features or may confuse similar services. Check the tool's official page.
verify.tools.tasks: Try tasks on practice examples, not important documents, until you understand how the tool behaves.
verify.tools.first: The first answer is rarely perfect. That's normal: refine the prompt and compare results.
verify.tools.compare: Pricing, limits and features change often. Check current terms on both tools' official sites.
verify.tools.check: Checking is your responsibility. The tool doesn't know where it went wrong.
verify.tools.settings: Setting names and locations change with updates. Check the tool's help pages.
verify.tools.safe: Don't enter passwords for other services, card details or documents, even if the tool asks. Check the site's address.
verify.tools.plan: Check pricing and availability by country only on the official site: AI often gets this wrong.
verify.tools.official: An official source is the developer's own site or help pages. Reviews and videos may be out of date.
verify.tools.changes: If a feature has gone or changed, first check the updates section on the official site.
